tuning.kurumamod.stroke.tooltip: How far the suspension can move. Longer is softer and soaks up bumps and landings; shorter is stiffer and sharper on tarmac. Spring rates are worked out from this and the spring sag.
tuning.kurumamod.static_sag.tooltip: How much of the travel the car sinks into when standing still. Higher means softer springs that let the wheels follow dips (good off-road). Lower is stiffer and sits the car higher.
tuning.kurumamod.body_clearance.tooltip: Height of the bottom of the body's collision box. The car looks the same. Raise it to stop the floor catching on steps and rocks; from 80 cm up, the car can climb a one-block step.
tuning.kurumamod.front_anti_roll.tooltip: Front anti-roll bar. Resists body roll in corners. A stiffer front bar loads the outer front tyre and makes the car push wide (understeer). 0 removes it.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_anti_roll.tooltip: Rear anti-roll bar. A stiffer rear bar makes the rear let go first, so the car turns in harder and can step out (oversteer). 0 removes it.
tuning.kurumamod.front_solid_axle.toolti: How the front wheels are carried. Independent: each wheel moves on its own. Solid axle: both wheels share one beam, so when one climbs a step the whole axle tilts. The other wheel stays planted on rocks and ledges, but the body leans more in corners.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_solid_axle.tooltip: How the rear wheels are carried. A solid axle keeps the diagonal wheel on the ground over steps. A solid rear alone shifts load toward the front in corners, so the car turns in a little less (understeer). The anti-roll bar works on the angle between axle and body; removing it lets the axle articulate even more.
tuning.kurumamod.front_roll_center.toolt: Front roll centre height, as a percentage of the centre of gravity. Higher means less roll and load reaching the front tyres sooner, which leans towards understeer.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_roll_center.toolti: Rear roll centre height, as a percentage of the centre of gravity. Higher means less roll and load reaching the rear tyres sooner, which leans towards oversteer.
tuning.kurumamod.front_bump_damping.tool: How firmly the front dampers resist compressing. Stronger slows nose dive under braking and the first moment of a turn, but bumps feel harsher.
tuning.kurumamod.front_rebound_damping.t: How firmly the front dampers resist extending. Stronger settles bouncing quickly, but too much keeps the tyre from following the road after a bump.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_bump_damping.toolt: How firmly the rear dampers resist compressing. Stronger slows the rear squatting under power, but bumps feel harsher.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_rebound_damping.to: How firmly the rear dampers resist extending. Stronger settles bouncing quickly, but too much leaves an unloaded rear tyre in the air longer.
tuning.kurumamod.friction.tooltip: How much grip the tyres have (1.00 is standard). More grip corners faster and stops shorter. Brake and handbrake strength follow this value.
tuning.kurumamod.tire_falloff.tooltip: How much grip is lost once the tyre slides past its peak. At 0 the grip stays; higher values make a slide harder to recover.
tuning.kurumamod.tire_load_sensitivity.t: How far grip falls short of rising with load. Higher values make weight transfer and the anti-roll bar balance matter more to how the car turns.
tuning.kurumamod.cornering_stiffness.too: How quickly the tyre builds sideways force. Higher feels sharper on the wheel, lower feels lazier. Maximum grip does not change.
tuning.kurumamod.wheel_radius.tooltip: Tyre size. Bigger tyres raise the car and climb taller steps (a lift kit). Gearing adjusts automatically, so acceleration and top speed stay the same.
tuning.kurumamod.mass.tooltip: How heavy the car is. Heavier cars accelerate and stop more slowly and are harder to change direction. Suspension stiffness follows the weight automatically.
tuning.kurumamod.weight_distribution.too: Share of the weight on the front wheels. Nose-heavy is stable and understeers; tail-heavy puts power down better and swings the rear more easily.
tuning.kurumamod.wheel_base.tooltip: Distance between the front and rear wheels. Longer is steadier at speed; shorter turns tighter and changes direction faster. Only the wheels move, not the body.
tuning.kurumamod.track_width.tooltip: Distance between the left and right wheels. Wider rolls less in corners and is harder to tip over. Only the wheels move, not the body.
tuning.kurumamod.rolling_resistance.tool: Resistance of the tyres rolling. Higher slows the car more when coasting and trims the top speed slightly.
tuning.kurumamod.drag_area.tooltip: Air resistance (drag coefficient × frontal area). Higher holds the car back at speed and lowers the top speed. About 0.5 for a sports car, 1.0 for an SUV.
tuning.kurumamod.max_steer.tooltip: How far the front wheels turn at full lock. More lock gives tighter turns and lets you hold deeper drift angles.
tuning.kurumamod.steer_grip_margin.toolt: How far past the grip limit the steering is allowed to go. 1.00 stops right at the limit; higher lets you over-steer into a slide, and 8.00 effectively turns this aid off.
How quickly the tyre builds driving and braking force. Lower values spin and lock the wheels more easily.
tuning.kurumamod.drive_layout.tooltip: Which wheels the engine drives. FF (front) is stable, FR (rear) steps out under power, and 4WD puts power down well on any surface.
tuning.kurumamod.torque_split.tooltip: In 4WD, the share of torque sent to the rear. Rear-biased turns under power like an FR; front-biased is more stable.
tuning.kurumamod.peak_torque.tooltip: The engine's strongest pull. More torque means harder acceleration. The power shown alongside is worked out from this and the rpm.
tuning.kurumamod.peak_torque_rpm.tooltip: Engine speed where peak torque arrives. Lower pulls hard from low revs; higher saves its punch for high revs.
tuning.kurumamod.peak_power_rpm.tooltip: Engine speed where peak power arrives. Its gap from the peak torque rpm shapes the torque curve; a wider gap keeps the pull going to higher revs.
tuning.kurumamod.idle_rpm.tooltip: Engine speed at idle. Pulling away starts from the torque at this speed, so raising it gives a slightly stronger launch.
tuning.kurumamod.redline_rpm.tooltip: Highest engine speed. A higher limit carries each gear to a higher speed. The automatic's shift points follow from it too.
tuning.kurumamod.engine_brake.tooltip: How hard the engine slows the car when you lift off. More engine braking slows you sooner and shifts weight forward off throttle.
tuning.kurumamod.engine_inertia.tooltip: How heavy the engine's spinning parts are (the flywheel). Lighter revs up and drops faster; heavier is smoother and slower.
tuning.kurumamod.gear_count.tooltip: Number of forward gears. More gears means a smaller rev drop on each shift and smoother acceleration.
tuning.kurumamod.first_gear.tooltip: 1st gear ratio. Higher gives a punchier launch but a lower top speed in 1st. It also sets how short the gearing is overall.
tuning.kurumamod.top_gear.tooltip: Top gear ratio. Lower reaches a higher top speed but pulls more weakly in top gear.
tuning.kurumamod.drivetrain_efficiency.t: Share of the engine's power that reaches the tyres. Lowering it dulls acceleration across the board.
tuning.kurumamod.shift_time.tooltip: How long a gear change takes. Drive is cut during the shift, so shorter changes keep acceleration going.
tuning.kurumamod.traction_control.toolti: Strength of the traction control that eases the throttle when the tyres spin. 0 turns it off. Turn it off to drift.
tuning.kurumamod.abs.tooltip: Strength of the anti-lock brakes. 0 turns them off. With ABS on you can still steer while braking hard.
tuning.kurumamod.diff_preload.tooltip: How much the limited-slip diff locks even with no throttle. More preload is steadier and calmer off throttle, but turns in less eagerly.
tuning.kurumamod.diff_lock_ratio.tooltip: How strongly the limited-slip diff locks under power. 0 is an open diff. Higher stops one wheel spinning away, and makes the rear step out under power.
tuning.kurumamod.diff_coast_ratio.toolti: How much the limited-slip diff locks off throttle, relative to on throttle. 0 is 1-way, 0.5 is 1.5-way, 1 is 2-way. Higher stops the car tucking in when you lift.
tuning.kurumamod.center_diff_lock.toolti: How tightly the front and rear axles are tied together in 4WD. 0 is free, 1 is locked. Tighter means less wheelspin but wider low-speed turns.
tuning.kurumamod.steer_rate.tooltip: Time to steer from one lock to the other with the keyboard. Longer makes small corrections easier; 0 is instant.
tuning.kurumamod.steer_return.tooltip: Time for the steering to return when you let go of the key. Shorter returns faster.
tuning.kurumamod.pedal_press.tooltip: Time to press the throttle and brake fully with the keyboard. Longer squeezes them on gently, which helps avoid wheelspin and lock-ups.
tuning.kurumamod.pedal_release.tooltip: Time to release the throttle and brake with the keyboard. Shorter lets go faster.
tuning.kurumamod.handbrake_press.tooltip: Time to pull the handbrake fully. 0 locks the rear wheels instantly.
tuning.kurumamod.self_aligning.tooltip: When you let go of the key, how strongly the steering returns to the direction of travel instead of the centre. Higher applies countersteer for you in a slide.
tuning.kurumamod.ackermann.tooltip: How much further the inside front wheel turns than the outside one. 100% is geometrically correct, 0% is parallel, negative is reversed. More helps tight low-speed turns.
tuning.kurumamod.front_toe.tooltip: Points the front wheels slightly in (positive, toe-in) or out (negative, toe-out). Toe-in steadies the car in a straight line; toe-out sharpens turn-in.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_toe.tooltip: Points the rear wheels slightly in (positive) or out (negative). Rear toe-in keeps the tail calmer at the limit.
tuning.kurumamod.front_roll_steer.toolti: How much the front wheels steer by themselves as the body rolls. Positive steers them outwards (understeer); negative steers them inwards (oversteer).
tuning.kurumamod.rear_roll_steer.tooltip: How much the rear wheels steer by themselves as the body rolls. Positive steers them with the fronts for stability (understeer); negative does the opposite (oversteer).
How far the front wheels steer as the bushes flex under cornering load (degrees per g). Positive makes them give way harder the harder you turn, for a gentle understeer at the limit.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_compliance_steer.t: How far the rear wheels steer as the bushes flex under cornering load (degrees per g). Positive steers them with the fronts, which settles the car in fast corners.
tuning.kurumamod.front_downforce.tooltip: Aerodynamic force pressing the front wheels down. It grows with speed and adds front grip. More than the rear makes the car oversteer at speed. It also adds some drag.
tuning.kurumamod.rear_downforce.tooltip: Aerodynamic force pressing the rear wheels down. It grows with speed and adds rear grip, steadying the car in fast corners. It also adds some drag.
tuning.kurumamod.manual_transmission.too: Automatic (AT) or manual (MT). In manual, R shifts up and F shifts down, and W/S are always throttle and brake.
tuning.kurumamod.visual_slip_limit.toolt: How far the front wheels can appear to point away from the direction of travel while drifting. Looks only; it does not change the handling. 0 turns it off.

config.kurumamod.title: KurumaMod Settings
config.kurumamod.show_help.tooltip: Shows the key/function list at the bottom right. Turn it off once you know the controls
config.kurumamod.camera_distance.tooltip: Blocks behind the car. Vanilla third person is fixed at 4, so higher values pull the view back.
config.kurumamod.camera_height.tooltip: 0 sits level with the car; higher values look down on it.
config.kurumamod.camera_speed_pull.toolt: Extra blocks to pull back at top speed. 0 keeps it constant. Pulling back makes the scenery flow slower, so raise "Speed FOV" below instead if you want more sense of speed.
config.kurumamod.speed_fov.tooltip: How many degrees to widen the view at full speed. 0 disables it. Scaled by what this car can reach, so a slow car widens just as much when flat out.
config.kurumamod.cockpit_look_ahead.tool: In first person, how far ahead along the path to look when cornering with grip (seconds). Higher shows more of the corner but turns the view sooner as you steer in. 0 disables it. Not used while drifting.
config.kurumamod.cockpit_drift_look.tool: In first person, how much to look toward the direction of travel while sliding. 0 keeps the view on the nose, 1 looks straight along the travel direction.
config.kurumamod.gauge_theme.tooltip: Same dials, different colours. Compare them while driving.
config.kurumamod.live_mirrors.tooltip: Heavy. To show the real view behind you, the world is rendered a second time every frame (roughly double the render cost, so expect lower fps). Only one mirror is refreshed per frame, so the cost does not grow with the number of mirrors. Does nothing unless the car model has mirrors. Turns itself off under Fabulous graphics and shader packs.
config.kurumamod.show_dust.tooltip: Smoke from tyres sliding on tarmac, and the dust the wheels tear off dirt, sand, gravel and snow. Both hang where they were thrown, so the car leaves a trail behind it. Rain stops the dust - though under a tunnel or bridge it keeps flying.
config.kurumamod.time_attack_ghost.toolt: In time attack, your best lap on the course drives alongside you as a see-through ghost, starting the moment you cross the line. It is replaced whenever you set a new personal best, and is deleted when you clear that best. Ghosts are saved on your computer only.
config.kurumamod.dust_density.tooltip: Multiplier for how much tyre smoke and dust is thrown. 1.0 is the default; it scales the particle count directly, so turn it down if it costs you frames. To switch it off entirely, use the toggle above.
config.kurumamod.show_own_skid_marks.too: Leave tyre marks on tarmac when the car you are driving slides (drifting, wheelspin, locked brakes).
config.kurumamod.show_other_skid_marks.t: Draw the tyre marks other players' cars leave. Empty cars and cars you ride in as a passenger count as other cars.
config.kurumamod.skid_mark_seconds.toolt: How many seconds a tyre mark stays before it disappears. It fades over the last 40%. Longer marks mean more of them on screen at once, which costs more to draw.
config.kurumamod.gate_display.tooltip: How much of each race gate to draw. Turn it down once you know the course.

config.kurumamod.show_gauges.tooltip: Draws round gauges and a shift indicator at the bottom of the screen. Separate from the telemetry numbers toggled with H
config.kurumamod.show_telemetry.tooltip: Lateral G, drift angle, surface and wheel loads in the bottom left. These are setup numbers - turn them off if you are just driving.

config.kurumamod.gauge_scale.tooltip: 1.0 by default. The gauges already shrink to fit the space beside the hotbar; this is your preference on top of that
config.kurumamod.gauge_opacity.tooltip: Opacity of the dial face and centre panel backdrop. 1.0 is opaque; lower values let the chat behind show through. Ticks and needles stay fully opaque
